Zeus.what: Hangs a stone over Tantalos, punishing his theft of nectar and ambrosia.
As Herakles' father, his precinct at Olympia receives the olive and the founded games.
Makes a cloud-snare to deceive Ixion, who is bound to a wheel.
Strikes Asklepios dead with lightning for raising a man from death.
Offers Polydeukes a choice, revives Kastor and destroys Idas with a thunderbolt.
Answers Herakles' prayer by sending an eagle as sign of Telamon's son.
Desires Thetis but yields her to Peleus after Themis's prophecy.

Apollo.what: Fathers Iamos and calls him to Kronion, granting prophecy and an oracle.
Helps build Troy's wall and reads the dragon sign as Troy's fall.
Snatches his unborn son Asklepios from Koronis's pyre and gives him to Cheiron.
Carries off the huntress Kyrene to Libya and questions Cheiron about her.

Herakles.what: Brings the olive from the Hyperboreans to Olympia and founds the games.
Kills the sons of Molos, destroys Augeas and founds the Olympic games.
Strangles Hera's snakes as an infant; Teiresias foretells his labors and bliss.
Likened to Melissos, he ends Antaios' killings in Libya.
Prays for a son for Telamon and names the child Aias.

Poseidon.what: Carries off Pelops, then gives him a golden chariot and winged horses.
Helps build Troy's wall with Apollo and Aiakos.
Desires Thetis but is warned off by Themis.

Achilles.what: Receives Cheiron's precept to honour Zeus and his parents.
Slays Memnon, glory of the Aiakidai.
Defeats Telephos, Memnon and Hektor and is mourned by the Muses.

Aiakos.what: Helps build Troy's wall and sees the dragons' omen.
Honoured at his shrine, where Pindar pleads as suppliant.

Peleus.what: Escapes Akastos' wife's plot and marries a Nereid.
Refuses Hippolyte's advances, is slandered, and wins Thetis.
Is given Thetis in marriage after Themis's prophecy.

Amphitryon.what: Rushes in with sword as Herakles strangles the snakes.

Athene.what: Gives Bellerophon the golden bridle to tame Pegasos.
Hears the Gorgon's lament and invents flute music.

Hera.what: Is the object of Ixion's lust; he embraces a cloud.
Sends two snakes against the infant Herakles.

Pindar.what: Promises Agesidamos a song and invokes the Muses.
Admits his forgotten debt and promises to repay with interest.
Counsels Arkesilas to heal Kyrene and recall Demophilos.
Offers his song as suppliant and promises a column of song for Meges' house.
Sets aside Apollo's song to honour Thebes and Herodotos.
Praises Lampon's house and promises the water of Dirke.

Adrastos.what: His praise of Amphiaraos is used to praise Agesias.
Flees Argos, reconciles with Amphiaraos, and leads the doomed Seven against Thebes.

Aias.what: Kills himself in anger over the arms of Achilles.
Is undone by envy and the vote for Odysseus.
Is named Aias by Herakles after the eagle sign.

Alkmene.what: Rushes in amazed as her infant Herakles strangles the snakes.

Cheiron.what: Receives Asklepios from Apollo to teach; Pindar wishes him alive.
Gives Achilles the precept to honour Zeus and parents.
Foretells Kyrene's future in Libya to Apollo.

Hieron.what: Wins at Olympia with his horse Pherenikos and is praised.
Praised for Pythian victory, wars, and advised to rule justly.
Praised for chariot win and rescue of the Lokrians; urged to honesty.
Ill, he is the object of Pindar's wish for Cheiron's healing.

Kastor.what: Attends Theron's feast with Polydeukes as honoured Twin.
Is killed by Idas, then revived through Polydeukes' shared immortality.

Leto.what: Gives birth on Delos, which pillars rise to support.

Thetis.what: Is won by Peleus after Themis's prophecy.

Agesidamos.what: Wins Olympic boxing victory and is promised a song.
Is praised after Pindar repays his forgotten debt.

Amphiaraos.what: Prophesies at Thebes on seeing Alkmaion.
Is swallowed by the earth at Thebes.

Muses.what: Invoked to join the triumph song for the Lokrians.

Persephone.what: Accepts atonement and sends souls back to the sun in the ninth year.

Perseus.what: Feasts among the Hyperboreans, led by Athene.
Kills Medusa and brings her head to Seriphos.

Polydeukes.what: Kills Lynkeus, begs to die with Kastor, and shares his immortality.

Telamon.what: Helps Herakles destroy Troy and slay Alkyoneus.
Hosts the feast where Herakles prays for his son.

Themis.what: Reveals that Thetis's son would surpass his father.

Arkesilas.what: Wins the chariot race and is urged to heal Kyrene.
Praised for Pythian chariot victory and prayed for to win Olympic crown.

Kadmos.what: Blessed at his wedding, later suffers grief.

Helios.what: Receives Rhodes rising from the sea as his portion.

Lampon.what: Praised for virtue as father of the athletes.

Melesias.what: Trainer Melesias praised with the Blepsiad family.
Praised at the ode's end as trainer.
Likened to a charioteer as trainer of Alkimidas.

Oinomaos.what: Is defeated by Pelops, who wins Hippodameia.

Pelops.what: Is carried off by Poseidon, then wins Hippodameia in the chariot race.

Pytheas.what: Wins the Nemean boys' pankration and is praised with his kin.
Trains his brother Phylakidas and is called for a crown.

Semele.what: Is killed by thunder and rises among the Olympians.
Is summoned to the Ismenian shrine to honour Thebes.

Thebe.what: Addressed as mother; Pindar puts Thebes before Delos.
Is addressed by Pindar, asked which of her deeds pleased most.

Theron.what: Wins Olympic chariot race and is praised for unmatched generosity.
Honours the Twins and reaches the pillars of Herakles.

Typhon.what: Lies bound beneath Etna, which erupts with fire and lava.

Bellerophon.what: Tames Pegasos with Athene's bridle and fights the Chimaira.
Is thrown by Pegasos when trying to reach heaven.

Antaios.what: Sets his daughter as prize in a foot-race.
Killed by Herakles, who ends his murders in Libya.

Asklepios.what: Born from Koronis's pyre, raised by Cheiron, he heals all but is struck down by Zeus.

Battos.what: The Pythian priestess hails Battos as king and tells him to found Kyrene.
Battos routes lions, founds Kyrene under Apollo's guidance, and is worshipped as hero after death.

Chromios.what: Chromios is praised for his chariot victory at Nemea, honoured in song at his house.
Chromios is celebrated for his Sikyon chariot victory and his courage in war by land and sea.

Hippodameia.what: Pelops wins Hippodameia by defeating Oinomaos with Poseidon's golden chariot and winged horses.

Hippolyte.what: Hippolyte slanders Peleus after he refuses her advances, as the Muses sing.

Jason.what: Jason claims his kingdom from Pelias, sails the Argo, yokes the bulls and wins the fleece.

Likymnios.what: Likymnios is killed in anger by Tlepolemos, who then flees to Rhodes.

Medea.what: Medea prophesies Kyrene's founding and helps Jason through his tasks at Colchis.

Medusa.what: Medusa is killed by Perseus, and her sisters' lament inspires Athena's flute.

Neoptolemos.what: Neoptolemos is killed at Delphi in a quarrel over meat and becomes the sanctuary's guardian.

Nestor.what: Nestor is saved from Memnon when his son Antilochos dies in his place.

Orestes.what: Orestes is saved by his nurse, raised by Strophios, and avenges Agamemnon.

Pegasos.what: Bellerophon tames Pegasos with Athene's bridle and uses him against the Chimaira.

Pherenikos.what: Pherenikos wins the Olympic race for Hieron and is praised by Pindar.

Phylakidas.what: Phylakidas is celebrated for his Isthmian victory, trained by his brother Pytheas.
Phylakidas, youngest son of Lampon, is honoured with a second bowl of song.

Psaumis.what: Psaumis is praised for his mule-chariot victory, horse-rearing, hospitality and civic peace.
Psaumis is praised for rebuilding Kamarina and wished a serene old age with his sons.

Teiresias.what: Teiresias prophesies Herakles' labors, victories over giants, and marriage to Hebe on Olympus.

Thrasyboulos.what: Thrasyboulos is praised as a dutiful son who honours his father and uses wealth wisely.
Thrasyboulos is addressed and urged to keep his father Xenokrates' fame alive.

Thrasydaios.what: Thrasydaios is honoured for his third Pythian victory, with his father.

Xenokrates.what: Xenokrates is honoured with a song-treasure at Delphi for his Pythian chariot victory.
Xenokrates is praised for his Isthmian win, other victories, kindness and hospitality.

Aietes.what: Aietes, king of Colchis, sets Jason tasks of the fire-breathing bulls and dragon.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon is murdered by Klytaimnestra on his return.

Agesias.what: Agesias, Olympic victor of Syracuse and Stymphalos, is praised and his song sent forth.

Aglaia.what: Aglaia, with the Graces, is hymned as giver of pleasant things at Orchomenos.

Aigisthos.what: Aigisthos is killed by Orestes in revenge.

Ainëas.what: Ainëas is sent as chorus leader to proclaim the song.

Aipytos.what: Aipytos raises Euadne and learns from Delphi of Iamos's destiny.

Alexidamos.what: Alexidamos wins the foot-race against rivals and leads Antaios' daughter away as his bride

Alkimedon.what: Alkimedon is celebrated as Aiginetan boy wrestler and Olympic victor, with his trainer and family praised

Alkimidas.what: Alkimidas wins the boy wrestling at Nemea, crowning his family's twenty-fifth victory

Alkmaion.what: Amphiaraos sees Alkmaion and prophesies; Pindar honors Alkmaion's grave as his neighbour

Antilochos.what: Antilochos dies in place of his father Nestor, saving him from Memnon

Aristagoras.what: Aristagoras is welcomed as prytanis of Tenedos and praised for sixteen victories and missed chances

Aristokleides.what: Aristokleides is celebrated for his Nemean pankration victory and receives the song as honeyed gift

Aristomenes.what: Aristomenes is praised as young Aiginetan wrestler who wins at Pytho and defeats rivals

Arsinoë.what: Arsinoë, Orestes' nurse, saves him while Klytaimnestra kills Agamemnon

Asopichos.what: Asopichos' Olympic victory is announced and Echo is sent to tell his dead father

Asopodoros.what: Asopodoros, Herodotos' father, is shipwrecked and finds shelter in Orchomenos

Augeas.what: Herakles destroys Augeas and his land after being cheated, then founds the games

Koronis.what: Koronis, pregnant by Apollo, takes another lover and is killed by Artemis; her child is rescued from the pyre

Deinis.what: Deinis is celebrated as young Nemean victor; Pindar approaches Aiakos' shrine as suppliant on his behalf

Demophilos.what: Exiled Demophilos is praised by Pindar, who hopes for his return to Kyrene

Deukalion.what: Deukalion and Pyrrha found the city of Opous after the flood

Diagoras.what: Diagoras, Rhodian boxer, is praised for his many victories and Zeus is asked to honour him

Dorieus.what: Dorieus, Diagoras' son, is freed by the Athenians, as the editor explains

Echo.what: Echo is sent to Persephone's home to tell Asopichos' father of his son's crown

Epharmostos.what: Epharmostos is celebrated for his wrestling victories across Greece and crowns Aias' altar

Ergoteles.what: Ergoteles, exiled from Knosos, wins at Olympia, Pytho and Isthmos, bringing glory to Himera

Euadne.what: Euadne secretly bears Apollo's child Iamos, who is fed by serpents among violets

Euphemos.what: Euphemos receives a clod from a god and loses it, delaying Libya's settlement
Euphemos sails with the Argonauts and his line reaches Kyrene via Lemnos

Theia.what: Pindar invokes Theia, mother of the Sun, and praises success and fame

Fortune.what: Fortune is invoked as saviour to protect Himera and rule the uncertainty of men's hopes

Herodotos.what: Herodotos wins the Isthmian chariot race and is honoured with praise and wishes for more wreaths

Hestia.what: Hestia is invoked to welcome Aristagoras and his colleagues at his installation as prytanis

Hippokleas.what: Hippokleas wins the boys' double race at Pytho and is praised with his family

Hypsipyle.what: After winning the armoured race, the son of Klymenos addresses Hypsipyle on Lemnos

Iamos.what: Iamos is born in secret to Euadne, fed by serpents among the violets
Iamos prays in the Alpheos and Apollo grants him prophecy at Olympia

Idas.what: Idas kills Kastor over oxen and is destroyed by Zeus's thunderbolt

Ischys.what: Ischys becomes Koronis's lover, and Koronis is killed for her unfaithfulness to Apollo

Ixion.what: Ixion lusts after Hera, embraces a cloud, is bound to a wheel, and fathers the Centaurs

Karrhotos.what: Karrhotos drives Arkesilas' winning chariot safely and dedicates his car at Delphi

Kassandra.what: Kassandra is killed with Agamemnon by Klytaimnestra

Kentauros.what: Kentauros is born of Ixion's union with the cloud

Kleandros.what: Kleandros is celebrated as pankratiast victor at Isthmos and Nemea

Klytaimnestra.what: Klytaimnestra kills Agamemnon and Kassandra, while Orestes is saved

Kyrene.what: Apollo carries off the huntress Kyrene to Libya after she fights a lion

Lynkeus.what: Lynkeus spots the twins and is killed by Polydeukes

Megakles.what: Megakles wins the Pythian victory and is praised with the Alkmaionidai, despite envy

Melissos.what: Melissos is praised for his pankration and chariot victories and likened to Herakles against Antaios

Midas.what: Midas, flute-player of Akragas, is welcomed with his Pythian victory crown

Nikesippos.what: Nikesippos is sent by Pindar to carry the ode to Thrasyboulos

Nikokles.what: Nikokles the boxer is praised with Kleandros for his victories

Oionos.what: Oionos wins the first stadion race at Olympia

Orseas.what: Orseas trains and guides Melissos to victory at the games for Herakles' sons

Paris.what: Paris strikes Nestor's horse, leaving Antilochos to die saving his father

Peace.what: Peace is hailed as daughter of Righteousness in Pindar's opening hymn

Pelias.what: Pelias meets Jason, then promises the throne if Jason fetches the fleece

Phintis.what: Phintis is called on to yoke the mules and carry the song

Phrastor.what: Phrastor wins the javelin at the first Olympic games

Pitane.what: Pitane's daughter Euadne bears Apollo's child, and Iamos is born among violets

Polydektes.what: Perseus brings Medusa's head to Seriphos for Polydektes' wedding

Porphyrion.what: Porphyrion is recalled as the giant who provoked Peace and fell

Rhodos.what: Rhodos, bride of Helios, bears his sons as the island rises from the sea

Samos.what: Samos of Mantinea wins the chariot race among the first Olympic victors

Sogenes.what: Sogenes is credited with his pentathlon victory through Eileithuia and Pindar's song
Pindar prays for Sogenes' family and defends his own honest praise

Son of Klymenos.what: After winning the armoured race on Lemnos, he tells Hypsipyle of his speed and heart

Strepsiades.what: Strepsiades wins the Isthmian pankration and shares glory with his fallen uncle

Strophios.what: Strophios shelters Orestes until he takes revenge

Tantalos.what: Tantalos is punished for stealing nectar and ambrosia from the gods

Telesikrates.what: Telesikrates wins the race in armour at Pytho, and Pindar proclaims his victory for Kyrene.

Theaios.what: Theaios is honoured as Pindar lists his many athletic wins and prays to Zeus for him.

Thersander.what: Thersander survives the house of Laïos's grief, wins honour and founds Theron's line.

Timasarchos.what: Timasarchos, young wrestling victor at Nemea, is celebrated for his wins and clan's glory.

Timodemos.what: Timodemos wins the Nemean pankration and is sung home by the citizens.

Tlepolemos.what: Tlepolemos kills Likymnios, consults the oracle, settles Rhodes and is honoured with games.

Xenophon.what: Xenophon wins the stadion and pentathlon at Olympia and is praised with his family.
